title: Rocket Rally brings 30-second arcade rally races to iOS and Android
summary: When we reviewed Major Mayhem, the iPhone 4S was brand new. Rocket Jump, the studio behind it, is back, this time with Rocket Rally, which is a physics-driven arcade rally racer that’s up for pre-registration on iOS and Android. If it predates your phone, Major Mayhem was a one-finger cover shooter. Your soldier ran between cover by himself, and you held a finger down to fire. It was brash and silly and very easy to pick up for a minute, and it also earned a Silver Award from us. ... [MORE]

title: Forgotten Memories: Definitive Edition is now free forever on iOS and Android
summary: Free forever is a big promise, but Psychose Interactive has a fairly good reason for making it. Forgotten Memories: Definitive Edition, the studio’s survival horror from 2015, is now free on iOS and Android. No, this isn’t a weekend giveaway or one of Epic Games' weekly freebies. It’s staying that way. You play as Rose Hawkins, who wakes up in an abandoned asylum while searching for a missing girl called Eden. It’s slow, third-person 90s-style horror, with puzzles, a torch and never quite enough ammo. ... [MORE]

title: Kettle Street sends you searching for a missing cat in its new Missing Abra event
summary: Where’s Wally (Waldo, if you grew up in the US) only works because everyone’s staring at the same page, so someone can point and the rest of you can pretend you’d nearly got there. Kettle Street, the cosy British life sim, is taking a page out of that book for their latest event, Missing Abra. Claire’s calico cat has gone missing somewhere in town, and you need to help find it. You find her by wandering Kettleby, and once you spot her, you take a photo with a new camera. She hides somewhere different in each person’s town, though. A mate who found her yesterday can’t tell you where yours is, and neither can we. No guides will help with this one. ... [MORE]

title: NBA 2K27 is out now on Apple Arcade, letting you manage your own NBA basketball team
summary: It's a big day for major league basketball fans. NBA 2K27: Arcade Edition has just landed on Apple Arcade, bringing the iconic basketball sim to mobile once more. And this time, it's more feature-rich than ever for newcomers and veterans alike. NBA 2K should need little introduction, even to those who don't know much about basketball or sports games in general. Allowing you to control both the management of your team and their actions on the field, it's to basketball what FIFA, or EA FC, is to football. Even better, with it on Apple Arcade you can take it all on the go! ... [MORE]

title: Talesweaver Mobile is Nexon's new MMO coming to Korea
summary: It would seem Nexon aren't content with just launching Temppal: Overgeared soon in certain regions, because they have another MMORPG on the cards too. TalesWeaver Mobile is another adaptation of a popular IP, and it's set to make its way to mobile in Korea, with sign-ups for its closed testing period now open. TalesWeaver originally launched in 2003 as an online RPG, a genre that was extremely popular in Korea and that gave rise to other hits such as MapleStory. This new spinoff takes you back to the world first outlined in Jeon Min-hee's novel Children of the Rune, with the familiar mix of fantastical world and colourful graphics. ... [MORE]

title: Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble doesn't make the grade and is set to be shut down
summary: Well, unfortunately, I think we all knew it was a strong possibility, but Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble, the PvP arena shooter spinoff of the hit PlayStation property, is officially cancelled. Service is set to end on May 1st 2027, with the game being delisted from stores on November 21st, with one final update to enjoy. Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble was a hero-style arena shooter, where you'd step into the shoes of new and existing characters from across the universe of Ratchet & Clank, duking it out in a combat simulation hosted by Captain Qwark to discover the next generation of Galactic Rangers. ... [MORE]

title: Ares: The Iron Vanguard's new update sees you and 15 other players take on a giant flying robot
summary: Ares: The Iron Vanguard offers a mashup of ARPG action and heavy metal fun with its giant power-suits and robotic enemies. Now, in its latest update, Ares: The Iron Vanguard is offering up brand-new cooperative content with the introduction of the Abyss Raid, which will challenge even the most experienced guilds already established! The Abyss Raid is a 15-player (yes, you read that right) cooperative boss battle against Arcarion, an enormous flying robot inspired by deep-sea creatures. You'll need to work together to evade its damaging abilities while destroying cores scattered around the battlefield to take down Arcarion before it takes down you. ... [MORE]

title: Dice of Kalma launches massive new 2.0 update with Dicebound Destiny
summary: Dice of Kalma, the Balatro-like dice roller, is already packed with stuff to do in this battle for your very soul. Now, it's set to get even bigger with the launch of its largest update yet, as Dice of Kalma's 2.0 version lands today, dubbed Dicebound Destiny, and for good reason! title: UnGodly shows off bloody good barbarian action in its new gameplay trailer
summary: Of all the upcoming releases we've covered, one that's kept my curiosity is UnGodly, the upcoming hack 'n slash RPG from Azra Games and Mark Otero, one of the key figures behind Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes. And in its most recent gameplay trailer, we not only got the announcement that it would be coming to iPhone Duo, but also a good look at its gameplay! It's easy to see why UnGodly is so consistently described as Frazetta-inspired, because everyone lacks a shirt, or at the very least seems to lack the buttons for them. But the action, as simple as it may seem, also benefits from some truly bloody gore effects as your heroes blast apart hapless mooks with everything from simple sword slashes to magic spells. ... [MORE]

title: The Roottrees are Dead has you investigating a complex family tree with 90s technology
summary: Mystery games tend to fall into very familiar divisions, with point-and-click adventures or hidden-object puzzlers as you attempt to unpack a mystery, such as a murder or disappearance. But The Roottrees are Dead offers a very different take on the format as it launches for iOS and Android, complete with an extra mystery! The Roottrees are Dead sees the story kick off with the deaths of the titular wealthy family, and your introduction in the role of investigator. Your job is not to figure out what killed them; that's already clear, but instead you have to track down their various relatives who, thanks to the wishes of an eccentric patriarch, are now entitled to a share of the enormous Roottree fortune. ... [MORE]

summary: Nowadays, crossovers are all the rage, be it in movies, comic books or television. And gaming is no different! Now, Kabam are set to tackle the back catalogue of one of entertainment's biggest companies, as WB All-Star Mayhem has been announced for iOS and Android! Set to start limited regional testing this month, WB All-Star Mayhem is a mobile RPG that sees the likes of everything from Adventure Time, Steven Universe, Samurai Jack and Scooby-Doo! cross over, as Animaniac's megalomaniacal mouse Brain gets his hands on a universal remote, with the intention of taking over each universe in turn unless someone puts a stop to him! ... summary: Of all the upcoming releases we've had our eyes on, one of the most interesting has been that of Honkai: Nexus Anima. MiHoYo's stab at a creature collector, mixed with their typical flashy ARPG action, has been slowly chugging along towards release for many months. Now, its final closed beta is set to go live on November 25th. summary: Once Human and its bizarre, paranormal world has played host to some strange seasons over its lifespan, most recently taking you into battle on the high seas against an enormous crab. Now, things are getting even stranger as Once Human's fifth season has been unveiled, titled Dissonant Resonance, set to land on November 19th. title: Crossy Road Rush sees the hit Frogger-like go full endless runner, out now on Apple Arcade
summary: Of all the games that take a concept that's already been done and turn it into a success, I think Crossy Road qualifies as one of the more successful. Hot off the back of Flappy Bird's success, Crossy Road Rush revamped the formula and combined it with Frogger to great effect. He’s heading to iOS and Android with the rest of this side-scrolling shoot ’em up, and to Switch as well. You’re stuck somewhere you don’t recognise, trying to get back to a Citadel in the sky, and the best thing you’ve got is a boat with an alarming amount of firepower bolted to it. Getting home means going through more than twenty mission types. Collision Course and Outlast explain themselves, while one is just called Boil. ... [MORE]

title: Old School RuneScape lets you test your mettle with the introduction of Hardcore Worlds
summary: Old School RuneScape and the whole RuneScape-verse has been going for nigh-on 20 years now, and for those looking for a challenge, there are plenty of bosses and dungeons to face. But now, even the most experienced of players can face a true trial, as today, Hardcore Worlds arrive in Old School RuneScape on all platforms, mobile included. Hardcore Worlds function exactly as you'd expect them to, but if you're new to the concept, here's a brief explainer: In Hardcore Worlds, death is final. As in no retries, no restarts. Whether it's slow or sudden, if your character perishes, you can either discard them or transfer them to a regular server, though without the rewards or goodies available exclusively on Hardcore Worlds. ... [MORE]

title: Monsta brings a turn-based portable classic to mobile, where it's you versus mutant monsters
summary: For many of us, the history of mobile gaming only stretches back to the first iPhone, and maybe a little further if we head back to the days of flip phones and the N-Gage. But look even further back, to when PDAs (Personal Digital Assistants) were all the craze, and you'll find examples of the primordial soup of mobile gaming, such as Monsta. First released back in the 2000s on PalmOS devices, and now available for the modern-day iOS and Android platforms, Monsta had to tackle many hardware limitations, including slow processing speed at the time. That's what inspired developer Superverse Industries to create this turn-based tactical shooter, where it's just you and a building full of monsters to get before they get you. ... [MORE]

title: Elder Scrolls: Sentinel has been named though not dated, but Elder Scrolls: Castles is here for a mobile fix
summary: Hallelujah! It seems that Bethesda Softworks have finally kicked themselves into gear, with the announcement that the hotly anticipated Elder Scrolls VI will be called Sentinel. And... Oh, turns out, that's all. Guess we're back to waiting, but if you need something to tide you over, did you know you can play The Elder Scrolls on mobile? Well, one of its spinoffs at the very least. With the shuttering of The Elder Scrolls: Blades earlier this year, options can seem thin on the ground. But dig a little deeper, and you'll find that Bethesda's The Elder Scrolls: Castles, which lets you build and manage your own fortress and family dynasty, offers you a hefty taste of Tamriel on the go!  ... [MORE]
